import Mathlib
import OAI.Probability.SKFluctuations.PositiveMass

namespace OAI

/-! Boundary Cost Congr. -/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology
open MeasureTheory Filter Set
open scoped Topology
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter Set
namespace SKFluctuations.Hierarchy
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter Set
open scoped Topology NNReal BigOperators

theorem boundaryCost_congr (as : List PositiveMass) {q r q' r' : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hq : ∀ j, j+1 < as.length → q j = q' j) (hr : ∀ j, j+1 < as.length → r j = r' j) :
    boundaryCost as q r = boundaryCost as q' r' := by
  induction as generalizing q r q' r' with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons a as ih =>
    cases as with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons b as =>
      simp only [boundaryCost]
      rw [hq 0 (by simp),hr 0 (by simp)]
      congr 1
      apply ih
      · intro j hj
        exact hq (j+1) (by simpa only [List.length_cons] using Nat.add_lt_add_right hj 1)
      · intro j hj
        exact hr (j+1) (by simpa only [List.length_cons] using Nat.add_lt_add_right hj 1)

theorem rootBoundaryCost_congr (as : List PositiveMass) {q r q' r' : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hq : ∀ j, j < as.length → q j = q' j) (hr : ∀ j, j < as.length → r j = r' j) :
    rootBoundaryCost as q r = rootBoundaryCost as q' r' := by
  cases as with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons a as =>
    simp only [rootBoundaryCost]
    rw [hq 0 (by simp),hr 0 (by simp)]
    congr 1
    exact boundaryCost_congr (a::as) (fun j hj => hq (j+1) hj) (fun j hj => hr (j+1) hj)

theorem rootBoundaryCost_uniform {as : List PositiveMass} {q r : ℕ → ℝ} {M : ℝ}
    (hM : 0 ≤ M) (ho : as.Pairwise (fun a b => a.val ≤ b.val))
    (hu : ∀ a ∈ as, a.val ≤ 1) (hm : ∀ j, j ≤ as.length → |q j-r j| ≤ M) :
    rootBoundaryCost as q r ≤ M := by
  cases as with
  | nil => exact hM
  | cons a as =>
    have hb := boundaryCost_le hM ho hu (q := fun j => q (j+1)) (r := fun j => r (j+1))
      (fun j hj => hm (j+1) (by omega))
    have h0 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hm 0 (by simp)) a.property.le
    change a.val*|q 0-r 0|+_ ≤ M
    nlinarith

namespace OAI

/-! Clock Root Marginal. -/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

open scoped Topology
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter Set
namespace SKFluctuations.Hierarchy.ClockTree
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter Set GaussianCalculus
open scoped NNReal BigOperators
variable {S : Type*} [Fintype S] [Nonempty S] {n : ℕ}

 theorem markedAttach_preserves {w : S → ℝ} (hw : ∀ σ, 0 < w σ)
    (φ : S → (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) {as : List PositiveMass}
    (T : ClockTree S as) {a : ℝ} (ho : MassOrdered a as)
    (p : MarkedPlacement T) (hp : p ∈ T.markedAttach a)
    (q : ℕ → Fin (n+1) → ℝ≥0) (P : T.Assignment → ℝ) (x : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) :
    p.tree.expect w φ q (fun σ => P (p.restrict σ)) x = T.expect w φ q P x := by
  have hm : p.realize q ∈ (T.realize q).markedAttach a := by
    rw [← T.markedAttach_realize a q]
    exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩
  have h := (T.realize q).markedAttach_preserves hw φ (clockSteps_ordered ho q)
    (p.realize q) hm (fun σ => P ((T.assignmentEquiv q).symm σ)) x
  rw [p.tree.expect_realize,T.expect_realize]
  simpa only [MarkedPlacement.realize,Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using h

 theorem rootExpect_integrable {w : S → ℝ} (hw : ∀ σ, 0 < w σ)
    (φ : S → (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) {as : List PositiveMass}
    (T : ClockTree S as) {a : ℝ} (ho : MassOrdered a as)
    (P : T.Assignment → ℝ) (q₀ : Fin (n+1) → ℝ)
    (q : ℕ → Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (x : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun y => T.expect w φ (fun j i => Real.toNNReal (q j i)) P (x+y))
      (Measure.pi fun i => gaussianReal 0 (Real.toNNReal (q₀ i))) := by
  have h := ((T.homTest P).eval_smooth hw φ ho q 0).integrable_zero_shift
    (ν := Measure.pi fun i => gaussianReal 0 (Real.toNNReal (q₀ i))) x
  simpa only [ClockTree.eval_homTest] using h

 theorem rootExpect_mono {w : S → ℝ} (hw : ∀ σ, 0 < w σ)
    (φ : S → (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) {as : List PositiveMass}
    (T : ClockTree S as) {a : ℝ} (ho : MassOrdered a as)
    {P Q : T.Assignment → ℝ} (hPQ : ∀ σ, P σ ≤ Q σ)
    (q₀ : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (q : ℕ → Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (x : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) :
    T.rootExpect w φ P q₀ q x ≤ T.rootExpect w φ Q q₀ q x := by
  rw [T.rootExpect_eq_integral,T.rootExpect_eq_integral]
  apply integral_mono (T.rootExpect_integrable hw φ ho P q₀ q x)
    (T.rootExpect_integrable hw φ ho Q q₀ q x)
  intro y
  dsimp only
  rw [T.expect_realize,T.expect_realize]
  exact (T.realize _).expect_mono hw φ (clockSteps_ordered ho _) (fun σ => hPQ _) _

# MODULE: expert_cache_residency
Slot arena bookkeeping of the VRAM expert cache: the per-layer slot ranges, the no-eviction admission counters
and the flat `(layer, expert)` residency index.

## Source semantics
- Layer `l` owns `[l*q, (l+1)*q)` with `q = slots / n_layers`; the last layer takes the remainder, so the ranges
  tile `0..slots` exactly.
- `admit` never evicts: a slot is handed out only while the counter is below the ceiling (global `slots_`, or the
  layer's own `hi`), and the counter then advances by one.
- The residency table is indexed `layer * n_expert + expert` and both axes are range-checked separately.

## Form template identifiers
- `layerLo`, `layerHi`  <- `ExpertCache::layer_slot_range` (lo, hi)
- `admitGlobal`         <- the shared `next_free_` path of `ExpertCache::admit`
- `admitLayer`          <- the `per_layer_` path (`layer_next_[layer]` against `hi`)
- `flatIdx`             <- `layer * n_expert_ + expert` into `residency_`
-/

namespace Strata.ExpertCache

/-- Lower bound of layer `l`'s slot range. -/
def layerLo (slots nl l : Nat) : Nat := l * (slots / nl)

/-- Upper bound (exclusive) of layer `l`'s slot range; the last layer takes the remainder. -/
def layerHi (slots nl l : Nat) : Nat := if l + 1 = nl then slots else (l + 1) * (slots / nl)

/-- Flat index into the residency table. -/
def flatIdx (ne layer expert : Nat) : Nat := layer * ne + expert

/-- Global compulsory-miss admission: returns the slot (if any) and the new counter. -/
def admitGlobal (next slots : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat :=
  if next < slots then (some next, next + 1) else (none, next)

/-- Per-layer admission against the layer's own ceiling `hi`. -/
def admitLayer (nxt hi : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat :=
  if nxt < hi then (some nxt, nxt + 1) else (none, nxt)

/-- The first layer's range starts at slot 0. -/
theorem layerLo_zero (s nl : Nat) : layerLo s nl 0 = 0 := by
  simp [layerLo]

/-- The last layer's range ends exactly at `slots`: no slot is orphaned by the division. -/
theorem layerHi_last (s nl l : Nat) (h : l + 1 = nl) : layerHi s nl l = s := by
  simp [layerHi, h]

/-- Adjacent ranges abut: layer `l`'s upper bound is layer `l+1`'s lower bound. -/
theorem layerHi_succ (s nl l : Nat) (h : l + 1 < nl) :
    layerHi s nl l = layerLo s nl (l + 1) := by
  have hne : ¬ (l + 1 = nl) := by omega
  simp [layerHi, layerLo, hne]

/-- Every in-range layer has a well-formed (possibly empty) range. -/
theorem layerLo_le_hi (s nl l : Nat) (h : l < nl) : layerLo s nl l ≤ layerHi s nl l := by
  unfold layerLo layerHi
  split
  · have h1 := Nat.mul_div_le s nl
    have h2 := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (s / nl) (show l ≤ nl by omega)
    omega
  · exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)

/-- A slot handed out by the global path is below the slot count. -/
theorem admitGlobal_lt (next slots s : Nat) (h : (admitGlobal next slots).1 = some s) : s < slots := by
  unfold admitGlobal at h
  split at h <;> simp_all

/-- The global counter never passes `slots`. -/
theorem admitGlobal_next_le (next slots : Nat) (h : next ≤ slots) :
    (admitGlobal next slots).2 ≤ slots := by
  unfold admitGlobal
  split <;> simp <;> omega

/-- A slot handed out by the per-layer path stays inside that layer's range. -/
theorem admitLayer_lt (nxt hi s : Nat) (h : (admitLayer nxt hi).1 = some s) : s < hi := by
  unfold admitLayer at h
  split at h <;> simp_all

/-- The per-layer counter never passes the layer's ceiling. -/
theorem admitLayer_next_le (nxt hi : Nat) (h : nxt ≤ hi) : (admitLayer nxt hi).2 ≤ hi := by
  unfold admitLayer
  split <;> simp <;> omega

/-- A full layer admits nothing (no eviction). -/
theorem admitLayer_full (nxt hi : Nat) (h : hi ≤ nxt) : (admitLayer nxt hi).1 = none := by
  unfold admitLayer
  have : ¬ (nxt < hi) := by omega
  simp [this]

/-- In-range `(layer, expert)` pairs land inside the residency table. -/
theorem flatIdx_lt (nl ne layer expert : Nat) (hl : layer < nl) (he : expert < ne) :
    flatIdx ne layer expert < nl * ne := by
  unfold flatIdx
  have h := Nat.mul_le_mul_right ne (Nat.succ_le_of_lt hl)
  simp only [Nat.succ_mul] at h
  omega

/-- The aliasing trap: expert id `ne` of layer 0 has the same flat index as expert 0 of layer 1,
so the expert axis must be validated separately from the flat index. -/
theorem flatIdx_alias (ne : Nat) : flatIdx ne 0 ne = flatIdx ne 1 0 := by
  simp [flatIdx]

end Strata.ExpertCache

# MODULE: expert_source_bounds

splits one layer's routed experts between GPU (hits) and CPU pool (jobs).

## Source semantics
- `blob(layer, expert)` returns a pointer only when both axes are in range and the flat index is below `blobs`.

- The artifact geometry is fixed: `experts.bin` holds exactly `48 * 512` blobs of 1,382,400 bytes.
- In the single-token dispatch, `njobs` indexes the job array and `i` the output; hits write zero rows and add
  no job, so `njobs = k - hits`.
- In a verify window the PCIe share is `(nmiss * pcie_num) >> 8`, never more than the missed experts.

## Form template identifiers
- `blobLookup`      <- `FileExpertSource::blob` / `ArenaExpertSource::blob` validity condition
- `hits`, `misses`  <- the `is_hit` / `host_res` split in `expert_pool_dispatch`
- `pcieShare`       <- `m = (nmiss * d.pcie_num) >> 8` in `expert_pool_dispatch_multi`
-/

namespace Strata.ExpertSource

/-- Blob index validity (layer unbounded above here: the flat index bound covers it). -/
def blobValid (ne blobs layer expert : Nat) : Prop :=
  expert < ne ∧ layer * ne + expert < blobs

/-- Number of hit entries in a per-index hit vector. -/
def hits : List Bool → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => (if b then 1 else 0) + hits t

/-- Number of miss entries (the jobs handed to the CPU pool). -/
def misses : List Bool → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => (if b then 0 else 1) + misses t

/-- PCIe share of the distinct missed experts. -/
def pcieShare (nmiss pcieNum : Nat) : Nat := (nmiss * pcieNum) / 256

/-- A valid blob request always has its expert id below the per-layer width. -/
theorem blobValid_expert_lt (ne blobs layer expert : Nat) (h : blobValid ne blobs layer expert) :
    expert < ne := h.1

/-- An id one past the end of a layer is refused even though its flat index may be in range. -/
theorem blobValid_rejects_overrun (ne blobs layer : Nat) : ¬ blobValid ne blobs layer ne := by
  intro h
  exact absurd h.1 (Nat.lt_irrefl ne)

theorem flat_collision (ne : Nat) : 0 * ne + ne = 1 * ne + 0 := by
  simp

/-- Every request of a valid geometry stays inside the pack. -/
theorem blobValid_in_pack (nl ne layer expert : Nat) (hl : layer < nl) (he : expert < ne) :
    layer * ne + expert < nl * ne := by
  have h := Nat.mul_le_mul_right ne (Nat.succ_le_of_lt hl)
  simp only [Nat.succ_mul] at h
  omega

  induction l with
  | nil => simp [hits, misses]
  | cons b t ih =>
    cases b <;> simp [hits, misses] <;> omega

  have h := hits_add_misses l
  omega

theorem misses_all_false (n : Nat) : misses (List.replicate n false) = n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [misses]
  | succ n ih =>
    simp only [List.replicate_succ, misses]

theorem pcieShare_le (nmiss pcieNum : Nat) (h : pcieNum ≤ 256) : pcieShare nmiss pcieNum ≤ nmiss := by
  unfold pcieShare
  have h2 : nmiss * pcieNum ≤ nmiss * 256 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left nmiss h

def widthOk (nEmbd : Nat) : Bool := decide (nEmbd = 2560)

/-- Width acceptance is exact. -/
theorem widthOk_iff (n : Nat) : widthOk n = true ↔ n = 2560 := by
  simp [widthOk]

end Strata.ExpertSource

# MODULE: layer_buffer_layout
Arena carving and structural checks of the composed layer (`layer.cpp`): 16-byte aligned buffer carving, Q8_K
sizing, the three-plane tensor consistency check, stage-selection flags of `block_layer_pre`, and the
GDN/QSA layer interleave.

## Source semantics
- Every buffer in a layer arena is rounded up to 16 bytes; a cursor never moves backwards.
- A Q8_K buffer holds `n/256` blocks of 292 bytes.
- A quantized tensor's codes + scales + offsets planes must add up to the tensor's byte count, and the offset
  flag must agree with the offset plane size.
- QSA layers are those with `layer % 4 == 3`: 12 of 48, leaving 36 GDN layers.
- `stage_prefix = k` runs stages `0..k-1`; `half = 0` runs everything, `1` the mixer, `2` the FFN front + router.

## Form template identifiers
- `align16`, `cursorTake` <- `(v + 15) & ~15`, `Cursor::take`
- `q8kBytes`              <- `q8k_bytes`
- `planesOk`              <- `plane_ptrs` consistency checks
- `runStage`, `runHalf`   <- `run0..run4` in `block_layer_pre`
- `isQsa`                 <- `is_qsa_layer`
-/

namespace Strata.Layer

/-- Round up to 16 (the `(v + 15) & ~15` of the carve loops). -/
def align16 (v : Nat) : Nat := (v + 15) / 16 * 16

/-- Cursor advance for `count` elements of `size` bytes. -/
def cursorTake (used count size : Nat) : Nat := align16 (used + count * size)

/-- Bytes of a Q8_K buffer of `n` elements. -/
def q8kBytes (n : Nat) : Nat := n / 256 * 292

/-- Plane consistency of a quantized tensor. -/
def planesOk (codes scales off total : Nat) (hasOffset : Bool) : Prop :=
  codes ≠ 0 ∧ scales ≠ 0 ∧ codes + scales + off = total ∧ (hasOffset = true ↔ off ≠ 0)

/-- Stage `i` runs under a stage prefix `k` (prefix mode). -/
def runStage (i k : Nat) : Bool := decide (i + 1 ≤ k)

/-- Stage `i` runs under `half` (0 = all, 1 = mixer, 2 = FFN front + router). -/
def runHalf (i half : Nat) : Bool :=
  if i < 3 then (half == 0 || half == 1) else (half == 0 || half == 2)

/-- QSA layer predicate. -/
def isQsa (l : Nat) : Bool := l % 4 == 3

/-- Aligned sizes are multiples of 16. -/
theorem align16_mod (v : Nat) : align16 v % 16 = 0 := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- Alignment never shrinks a buffer. -/
theorem align16_ge (v : Nat) : v ≤ align16 v := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- Alignment wastes fewer than 16 bytes. -/
theorem align16_lt (v : Nat) : align16 v < v + 16 := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- A cursor take never moves the cursor backwards and covers the requested bytes. -/
theorem cursorTake_covers (used count size : Nat) : used + count * size ≤ cursorTake used count size := by
  unfold cursorTake
  have := align16_ge (used + count * size)
  exact this

/-- A cursor that started 16-aligned stays 16-aligned. -/
theorem cursorTake_mod (used count size : Nat) : cursorTake used count size % 16 = 0 := by
  unfold cursorTake
  exact align16_mod _

/-- The activation row of the model's width needs 10 Q8_K blocks (2920 bytes). -/
theorem q8kBytes_2560 : q8kBytes 2560 = 2920 := by
  decide

/-- A Q8_K buffer for a multiple of 256 holds whole blocks. -/
theorem q8kBytes_blocks (n : Nat) (h : n % 256 = 0) : q8kBytes n = (n / 256) * 292 := by
  rfl

/-- Consistent planes lie wholly inside the tensor: the scales plane ends at or before the offset plane. -/
theorem planesOk_in_bounds (c s o t : Nat) (b : Bool) (h : planesOk c s o t b) : c + s ≤ t := by
  obtain ⟨_, _, h3, _⟩ := h
  omega

/-- A tensor with an offset plane declares `has_offset`, and conversely. -/
theorem planesOk_offset_flag (c s o t : Nat) (b : Bool) (h : planesOk c s o t b) (ho : o ≠ 0) :
    b = true := by
  obtain ⟨_, _, _, h4⟩ := h
  exact h4.mpr ho

/-- Running the first `k` stages means stage `i` runs exactly when `i < k`. -/
theorem runStage_iff (i k : Nat) : runStage i k = true ↔ i < k := by
  simp [runStage]
  omega

/-- A prefix of 5 runs every one of the five stages. -/
theorem runStage_full (i : Nat) (hi : i < 5) : runStage i 5 = true := by
  rw [runStage_iff]; exact hi

/-- Stage prefixes are monotone: a longer prefix runs everything a shorter one does. -/
theorem runStage_mono (i k k' : Nat) (h : k ≤ k') (hr : runStage i k = true) : runStage i k' = true := by
  rw [runStage_iff] at *
  omega

/-- `half = 0` runs every stage. -/
theorem runHalf_all : ∀ i : Fin 5, runHalf i.val 0 = true := by
  decide

/-- The two halves together cover every stage. -/
theorem runHalf_cover : ∀ i : Fin 5, (runHalf i.val 1 || runHalf i.val 2) = true := by
  decide

/-- The two halves never run the same stage twice. -/
theorem runHalf_disjoint : ∀ i : Fin 5, (runHalf i.val 1 && runHalf i.val 2) = false := by
  decide

/-- Exactly 12 of the 48 layers are QSA. -/
theorem qsa_count : ((List.range 48).filter (fun l => isQsa l)).length = 12 := by
  decide

/-- Exactly 36 of the 48 layers are GDN. -/
theorem gdn_count : ((List.range 48).filter (fun l => !isQsa l)).length = 36 := by
  decide

/-- The RoPE position guard: an accepted position lies below the table size. -/
theorem rope_pos_in_table (posBase pos maxCells : Nat) (h : posBase + pos < maxCells) : pos < maxCells := by

GDN/QSA layer interleave.

- Every buffer in a layer arena is rounded up to 16 bytes; a cursor never moves backwards.
- A Q8_K buffer holds `n/256` blocks of 292 bytes.
- A quantized tensor's codes + scales + offsets planes must add up to the tensor's byte count, and the offset
  flag must agree with the offset plane size.
- QSA layers are those with `layer % 4 == 3`: 12 of 48, leaving 36 GDN layers.
- `stage_prefix = k` runs stages `0..k-1`; `half = 0` runs everything, `1` the mixer, `2` the FFN front + router.

- `align16`, `cursorTake` <- `(v + 15) & ~15`, `Cursor::take`
- `q8kBytes`              <- `q8k_bytes`
- `planesOk`              <- `plane_ptrs` consistency checks
- `runStage`, `runHalf`   <- `run0..run4` in `block_layer_pre`
- `isQsa`                 <- `is_qsa_layer`

/-- Round up to 16 (the `(v + 15) & ~15` of the carve loops). -/

/-- Cursor advance for `count` elements of `size` bytes. -/
def cursorTake (used count size : Nat) : Nat := align16 (used + count * size)

/-- Bytes of a Q8_K buffer of `n` elements. -/
def q8kBytes (n : Nat) : Nat := n / 256 * 292

/-- Plane consistency of a quantized tensor. -/
def planesOk (codes scales off total : Nat) (hasOffset : Bool) : Prop :=
  codes ≠ 0 ∧ scales ≠ 0 ∧ codes + scales + off = total ∧ (hasOffset = true ↔ off ≠ 0)

/-- Stage `i` runs under a stage prefix `k` (prefix mode). -/
def runStage (i k : Nat) : Bool := decide (i + 1 ≤ k)

/-- Stage `i` runs under `half` (0 = all, 1 = mixer, 2 = FFN front + router). -/
def runHalf (i half : Nat) : Bool :=
  if i < 3 then (half == 0 || half == 1) else (half == 0 || half == 2)

/-- QSA layer predicate. -/
def isQsa (l : Nat) : Bool := l % 4 == 3

/-- Aligned sizes are multiples of 16. -/
theorem align16_mod (v : Nat) : align16 v % 16 = 0 := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- Alignment never shrinks a buffer. -/
theorem align16_ge (v : Nat) : v ≤ align16 v := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- Alignment wastes fewer than 16 bytes. -/
theorem align16_lt (v : Nat) : align16 v < v + 16 := by
  unfold align16; omega

theorem cursorTake_covers (used count size : Nat) : used + count * size ≤ cursorTake used count size := by
  unfold cursorTake
  have := align16_ge (used + count * size)
  exact this

  unfold cursorTake
  exact align16_mod _

  obtain ⟨_, _, h3, _⟩ := h
  omega

  omega

  decide

  decide

theorem rope_pos_in_table (posBase pos maxCells : Nat) (h : posBase + pos < maxCells) : pos < maxCells := by

theorem k_guard (k : Nat) (h1 : 1 ≤ k) (h2 : k ≤ 64) : 0 < k ∧ k < 65 := by
  omega

- `qsaBefore`   <- count of QSA layers before `l` (the `gdn_index` loop complement)
- `gdnIndex`    <- `gdn_index` in `gdn_point_at` / `session_token`
- `ringWant`    <- `want = ++expected` in `session_loop`, `(uint32_t)(l + 1)` in `session_run_token`
-/

  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => qsaBefore n + (if n % 4 = 3 then 1 else 0)

/-- The doorbell sequence value layer `l` waits for. -/

/-- Floats of one GDN layer's recurrence plus conv history. -/

  unfold alignUp256; omega

  unfold alignUp256; omega

  unfold sessionTake
  exact alignUp256_mod _

# MODULE: weight_loader_segments
Byte accounting of the dense-weight loader: per-plane segment sums with fp16 scale widening, chunked
conversions (BF16 high-half, f16 widening) and their staging-buffer bounds, and the compacted arena layout.

## Source semantics
- A quantized tensor is codes, scales and an optional offset plane. With fp16 scales the source scale plane is
  half the destination plane; the segment sums are checked against the index totals.
- Chunks are at most 8 MiB of source. BF16 conversion maps 4 source bytes to 2; f16 widening maps 2 to 4, so
  the output staging buffer is twice the input one.
- Destination offsets inside a converted run are `done / 2` (shrinking) or `done * 2` (widening).
- A skip set compacts the arena: kept rows are placed at 256-aligned running offsets.

## Form template identifiers
- `srcSum`, `dstSum` <- `sum_src`, `sum_dst`
- `widenOut`, `bf16Out` <- `out_bytes = (n/2)*4` and `(n/4)*2`
- `placeNext`        <- `at += (dst_bytes + a - 1) / a * a`
-/

namespace Strata.Weights

/-- Source bytes of a quantized tensor's three planes. -/
def srcSum (codes scales off : Nat) (fp16 : Bool) : Nat :=
  codes + (if fp16 then scales / 2 else scales) + off

/-- Destination bytes of the three planes. -/
def dstSum (codes scales off : Nat) : Nat := codes + scales + off

/-- Output bytes of widening `n` source bytes of fp16 to f32. -/
def widenOut (n : Nat) : Nat := (n / 2) * 4

/-- Output bytes of taking the high half of `n` source bytes of f32. -/
def bf16Out (n : Nat) : Nat := (n / 4) * 2

/-- Next compacted placement offset (alignment 256). -/
def placeNext (at_ bytes : Nat) : Nat := at_ + (bytes + 255) / 256 * 256

/-- Without fp16 scales the source and destination sums agree. -/
theorem srcSum_eq_dstSum (c s o : Nat) : srcSum c s o false = dstSum c s o := by
  simp [srcSum, dstSum]

/-- Widening can only grow the plane: the source sum never exceeds the destination sum. -/
theorem srcSum_le_dstSum (c s o : Nat) (fp : Bool) : srcSum c s o fp ≤ dstSum c s o := by
  unfold srcSum dstSum
  split <;> omega

/-- With an even fp16 scale plane the source is exactly half of the destination plane. -/
theorem fp16_half (s : Nat) (h : s % 2 = 0) : (s / 2) * 2 = s := by
  omega

/-- Widening an even run doubles its byte count. -/
theorem widenOut_double (n : Nat) (h : n % 2 = 0) : widenOut n = 2 * n := by
  unfold widenOut; omega

theorem widen_fits (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ 8388608) : widenOut n ≤ 2 * 8388608 := by
  unfold widenOut; omega

  unfold bf16Out; omega

/-- The BF16 output fits the staging buffer. -/
theorem bf16_fits (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ 8388608) : bf16Out n ≤ 2 * 8388608 := by
  unfold bf16Out; omega

/-- A chunk size is a multiple of 4 (so converted chunks never split an element). -/
theorem chunk_mod4 : 8388608 % 4 = 0 := by
  decide

/-- Consecutive BF16 chunks tile the destination: the next chunk starts where this one's output ends. -/
theorem bf16_chunks_tile (done n : Nat) (hd : done % 4 = 0) (hn : n % 4 = 0) :
    done / 2 + bf16Out n = (done + n) / 2 := by
  unfold bf16Out; omega

/-- Consecutive widening chunks tile the destination. -/
theorem widen_chunks_tile (done n : Nat) (hd : done % 2 = 0) (hn : n % 2 = 0) :

  unfold widenOut; omega

/-- Only exactly 19 parsed fields pass. -/
theorem rowOk_iff (n : Nat) : rowOk n = true ↔ n = 19 := by
  simp [rowOk]

end Strata.Weights

# MODULE: direct_file_requests
Request validation and completion draining of the unbuffered direct-I/O file reader.

## Source semantics
- A request is accepted only when its offset, length and buffer address are all multiples of the device
  alignment and the length is non-zero.
- `wait(out, max)` first drains queued immediate completions and never returns more than `max`.
- A POSIX read completes inside `submit`; its completion is `ok` exactly when `pread` did not fail, and carries
  zero bytes on failure.
- A STATUS_END_OF_FILE completion is a legal short read, treated as ok.

## Form template identifiers
- `reqValid`   <- the alignment test at the head of `DirectFile::submit`
- `drained`    <- number of completions written by `DirectFile::wait`
- `posixDone`  <- the `Completion{tag, got < 0 ? 0 : got, got >= 0}` of the POSIX `submit`
-/

namespace Strata.DirectFile

/-- A request is valid when offset, length and address are aligned and the length is non-zero. -/
def reqValid (a off len addr : Nat) : Prop :=
  off % a = 0 ∧ len % a = 0 ∧ addr % a = 0 ∧ len ≠ 0

/-- Completions returned by one `wait`: the queue is drained up to `max`. -/
def drained (max queued : Nat) : Nat := min max queued

/-- POSIX completion bytes and ok flag for a signed `pread` result. -/

  obtain ⟨_, h2, _, h4⟩ := h
  exact Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h4) (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h2)

  simp

/-!
# MODULE: direct_file_requests
Request validation and completion draining of the unbuffered direct-I/O file reader.

## Source semantics
- A request is accepted only when its offset, length and buffer address are all multiples of the device
  alignment and the length is non-zero.
- `wait(out, max)` first drains queued immediate completions and never returns more than `max`.
- A POSIX read completes inside `submit`; its completion is `ok` exactly when `pread` did not fail, and carries
  zero bytes on failure.
- A STATUS_END_OF_FILE completion is a legal short read, treated as ok.

## Form template identifiers
- `reqValid`   <- the alignment test at the head of `DirectFile::submit`
- `drained`    <- number of completions written by `DirectFile::wait`
- `posixDone`  <- the `Completion{tag, got < 0 ? 0 : got, got >= 0}` of the POSIX `submit`
-/

namespace Strata.DirectFile

/-- A request is valid when offset, length and address are aligned and the length is non-zero. -/
def reqValid (a off len addr : Nat) : Prop :=
  off % a = 0 ∧ len % a = 0 ∧ addr % a = 0 ∧ len ≠ 0

/-- Completions returned by one `wait`: the queue is drained up to `max`. -/
def drained (max queued : Nat) : Nat := min max queued

/-- POSIX completion bytes and ok flag for a signed `pread` result. -/
def posixDone (got : Int) : Nat × Bool := (if got < 0 then 0 else got.toNat, decide (0 ≤ got))

/-- A valid request transfers at least one alignment unit. -/
theorem reqValid_len_ge (a off len addr : Nat) (h : reqValid a off len addr) : a ≤ len := by
  obtain ⟨_, h2, _, h4⟩ := h
  exact Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h4) (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h2)

/-- The end of a valid request is aligned too, so consecutive requests tile the file. -/
theorem reqValid_end_aligned (a off len addr : Nat) (h : reqValid a off len addr) :
    (off + len) % a = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, _, _⟩ := h
  rw [Nat.add_mod, h1, h2]
  simp

/-- A zero-length request is never valid. -/
theorem reqValid_not_zero (a off addr : Nat) : ¬ reqValid a off 0 addr := by
  intro h
  exact h.2.2.2 rfl

/-- `wait` never returns more than the caller's buffer holds. -/
theorem drained_le_max (max queued : Nat) : drained max queued ≤ max :=
  Nat.min_le_left max queued

/-- `wait` never returns more completions than were queued. -/
theorem drained_le_queued (max queued : Nat) : drained max queued ≤ queued :=
  Nat.min_le_right max queued

/-- If the buffer is large enough the queue is emptied. -/
theorem drained_all (max queued : Nat) (h : queued ≤ max) : drained max queued = queued := by
  unfold drained
  omega

/-- A failed `pread` yields a zero-byte, not-ok completion. -/
theorem posixDone_fail (got : Int) (h : got < 0) : posixDone got = (0, false) := by
  unfold posixDone
  have : ¬ (0 ≤ got) := by omega
  simp [h, this]

/-- A successful `pread` yields an ok completion with exactly the bytes read. -/
theorem posixDone_ok (got : Int) (h : 0 ≤ got) : posixDone got = (got.toNat, true) := by
  unfold posixDone
  have : ¬ (got < 0) := by omega
  simp [this, h]

end Strata.DirectFile
